subject: general
question: A and B can do a job in 25 days and 18 days, respectively. A works alone for 4 days and leaves. The number of days required by B to complete the remaining job is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 25, 18) = 450 units

Efficiency: A = 18 units/day, B = 25 units/day

Work done by A in 4 days = 18 × 4 = 72 units

Remaining work = 450 − 72 = 378 units

Days taken by B = 378 ÷ 25 = 15 (3/25) days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 (3/25) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 25 days, Time taken by **B** = 18 days. **A** worked for 4 days.

**Formula Used:** Work = Efficiency × Time; Remaining Work = Total Work − Work Done.

 **Person**
 **Days**

 **Efficiency**

 **A**

 18

⇒ Total Work = LCM(25, 18) = 450 units

⇒ Work completed by **A** in 4 days = 18 × 4 = 72 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 450 − 72 = 378 units

⇒ Days required by **B** = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Days = 378 ÷ 25

⇒ Days = 15 (3/25) days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 (3/25) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a job. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Remaining Work Concept

When a person leaves, the **Remaining Work** must be divided by the **Efficiency** of the person staying to find the additional time required.

LCM Method

Using the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given days as the total work simplifies calculation by avoiding fractions until the final step.</p
